summary: Both build_seriality_constraint and build_interpolation_constraint implemented (Skolemized, no z3.Exists), wired into build_frame_constraints, docstrings corrected, ARCHITECTURE.md ledger added, and the full 52-example regression run completed with every flip explained. Landing is blocked by a well-evidenced but not-fully-mechanistically-understood cost regression: BM_CM_4 (N=2,M=2 countermodel) goes from 4.07s decided match to inconclusive at its own max_time=120 with both axioms present, confirmed by four independent measurements against the real committed methods. BM_CM_1 shows the same before/after direction but its own isolation table is non-monotonic (its 'both' configuration is faster than 'neither'), which rules out asserting a single general interaction mechanism -- that hypothesis is explicitly not claimed as established. Full bimodal suite: 308 passed, 5 failed, all attributable to these two examples. The broader code/tests/ suite was not run in this session (recorded, not assumed clean). No axiom was dropped, no timeout raised, no test marked unstable, and no expected verdict adjusted to route around the finding -- per explicit team-lead guidance during implementation, both axioms remain in the code as specified pending the user's landing decision.

blockers.description: BM_CM_4 regresses from a clean, fast, decided countermodel (4.07s match pre-change) to inconclusive at its own max_time=120s with both new axioms present. Reproduced in 4 independent measurements against the real committed methods (pytest 120.78s FAILED; direct call 120.37s inconclusive; full-suite run 120.36s inconclusive; 40s-budget probe 40.21s inconclusive). Cost regression, not a shown soundness/verdict flip.
blockers.attempted_remediation: Isolation shows neither axiom alone is responsible (both individually stay decided, ~2-3x baseline cost). One mitigation (explicit Z3 pattern anchoring Interpolation to its premise's ground term, mirroring forward_comp's existing MultiPattern) did not recover a decided result. Guard-tightening not attempted separately -- both guards are already as tight as their mathematical content allows.
blockers.user_decision_needed: Accept the regression and land both axioms as-is; apply the plan's own documented fallback (land Seriality alone, defer Interpolation) even though isolation does not identify Interpolation alone as the cause; or spawn a follow-on task for a repeated-runs variance study before deciding.

blockers.description: BM_CM_1 shows the same before/after direction (match->inconclusive) but its own isolation table is non-monotonic and contradicts BM_CM_4's pattern (its 'both' configuration decides faster than 'neither'; its 'interpolation_only' configuration is the one that fails to decide). This rules out a single general 'superlinear interaction' mechanism claim across both examples.
blockers.attempted_remediation: Not investigated further within this session's budget; BM_CM_1's own unstable marker and documented heavy-tail baseline (22.55s vs. its ~7-8s median in this very isolation run) mean this is corroboration of high solver-cost variance as much as an axiom-specific effect.
blockers.user_decision_needed: Whether a repeated-runs variance study (out of this task's budget) is warranted to settle the mechanism before any landing decision.

decisions_made: Did not apply the plan's own documented rollback fallback (land Seriality alone, defer Interpolation) unilaterally: isolation shows neither axiom alone is individually responsible for BM_CM_4's regression, and dropping one axiom would silently narrow this task's shipped scope (both axioms asserted, per the task's own definition of done) without the user's decision.

Ran Phase 7's post-change regression using the harness's baseline arm (real committed core.py methods) rather than the with_new_axioms arm (a script-local inline reconstruction) after discovering the two diverge on BM_CM_4 due to Z3 MBQI sensitivity to symbol naming -- the inline reconstruction falsely showed no regression (4.56s match) while the real methods reproducibly time out (120s+).

Explicitly declined to state 'the two axioms interact superlinearly' as an established mechanism after BM_CM_1's isolation table contradicted BM_CM_4's monotonicity pattern -- reported as a corroborated-but-unsettled hypothesis instead, with the repeated-runs study needed to settle it named as a follow-on.

Did not raise BM_CM_4's or BM_CM_1's max_time, mark either test unstable/xdist_serial, adjust either example's expected verdict, or drop an axiom to restore a green suite -- all four were explicit standing constraints during implementation and are preserved in the final code.
Did not run the broader code/tests/ suite in this session given the time budget; recorded as an open item rather than assumed clean.
